description:
FILED s515a (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-11) from the #3184 guard negatives.

    BEGIN { my $m = "TagMod"; eval "use $m qw(f0)" }   # f0 has prototype ($)
    my @x = ("a", "b"); print f0(@x), "\n";
perl 5.40.3: f0(2) (the import ran at BEGIN, before the call was parsed).  PCL: f0(a,b) -- the body is computed, so the static read (Pl::Parser::use_statements_of, literal shape only) cannot see it, and PCL_DETECT=announce prints NOTHING for this site (the detector does not see an install made by a string eval?).  Fixture: Pl/t/lib/TagMod.pm.  Two halves: (a) why the detector is silent here; (b) whether anything static is possible (no -- a computed name; the detector is the route).
subject: a sub imported by a COMPUTED BEGIN-time string eval (BEGIN { my $m = 'M'; eval "use $m qw(f)" }) is parsed without its prototype, and the #2610 detector does not name the site
